newsitem.title: CROATIA: Three people shot during burglary in Serb region.
newsitem.headline: Three people shot during burglary in Serb region.

text.p: Three people of mixed ethnic origin were killed during a house burglary that went wrong in the volatile Serb-held Eastern Slavonia area, a United Nations official said on Tuesday.
"We believe the incident was a burglary that went wrong and three persons were killed -- a husband and wife and grandmother of mixed ethnic origin," a U.N. source said.
The area is under Transitional Administration (UNTAES) until July 15, when it is supposed to come back under Zagreb's rule.
The incident happened in the town of Beli Manastir in the far northeast of Croatia on Monday night, and witnesses described the perpetrator as an armed man wearing a camouflage fatigue and a mask.
The murdered couple was of mixed Hungarian-Serb origin, and the U.N. source said they did not believe there was a political motive.
Eastern Slavonia, the last Serb-held enclave, is due to revert to Zagreb's control later this year.
Increasing violence, including a series of bombing and shooting incidents in which a Belgian U.N. soldier was killed, has raised tensions over the past few months.

The Croatian government is expected to announce later this week the exact date of the local elections to be held in the whole of the country, including Eastern Slavonia which would complete the region's reintegration.
Local Serbs and the Yugoslav army took control of the wealthy farming region in 1991, rebelling against a Croatian bid for independence from the former Yugoslav federation.
